# curl2 (Resource)

Manages an object behind a REST API with a request on create, and optional requests on read, update and destroy. Any response outside 200-299 fails the operation. `{id}` in the read, update and destroy `uri` or `json` is replaced with the ID taken from the create response.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    curl2 = {
      source  = "mehulgohil/curl2"
      version = "1.8.0"
    }
  }
}

provider "curl2" {}

variable "api_token" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

# A webhook managed through a REST API.
resource "curl2" "webhook" {
  auth_type    = "Bearer"
  bearer_token = var.api_token

  # Where the new object's ID is in the create response, e.g. {"data": {"id": 42}}.
  id_path = "data.id"

  create = {
    uri  = "https://api.example.com/hooks" # POST by default
    json = jsonencode({ url = "https://example.com/hook", events = ["push"] })
  }

  # Optional: refresh. A 404 or 410 means it was deleted outside Terraform, so it is created again.
  read = {
    uri = "https://api.example.com/hooks/{id}" # GET by default
  }

  # Optional: in-place update. Without it, a change to create replaces the object.
  update = {
    uri  = "https://api.example.com/hooks/{id}" # PUT by default
    json = jsonencode({ url = "https://example.com/hook", events = ["push"] })
  }

  # Optional: without it, destroy only removes the object from state.
  destroy = {
    uri = "https://api.example.com/hooks/{id}" # DELETE by default
  }
}

output "webhook_id" {
  value = curl2.webhook.id
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `create` (Attributes) Request sent on create. If `update` is not set, any change to `create` replaces the object (destroy, then create). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--create))

### Optional

- `auth_type` (String) Authentication Type, Bearer or Basic.
- `basic_auth_password` (String, Sensitive) Password to be used for Authentication.
- `basic_auth_username` (String) Username to be used for Basic Authentication.
- `bearer_token` (String, Sensitive) Bearer Token to be used for Authentication.
- `destroy` (Attributes) Request sent on destroy. A 404 or 410 response counts as success. If not set, destroy only removes the object from state. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--destroy))
- `headers` (Map of String) Headers sent with every request.
- `id_path` (String) Where the ID is in the create response JSON, as a dot path such as `id`, `data.id` or `items.0.id`.
- `read` (Attributes) Request sent on refresh. A 404 or 410 response means the object was deleted outside Terraform, and it is created again. If not set, refresh sends no request. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--read))
- `update` (Attributes) Request sent when `create` or `update` changes. If not set, those changes replace the object. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--update))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The object's ID: the value at `id_path` in the create response, or a hash of the create request if `id_path` is not set.
- `response` (Attributes) Response of the last create, update or read request. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--response))

<a id="nestedatt--create"></a>
### Nested Schema for `create`

Required:

- `uri` (String) URI to send the request to. `{id}` is replaced with the resource ID (not in `create`).

Optional:

- `http_method` (String) HTTP method. Defaults to POST.
- `json` (String) JSON body in string format, e.g. from `jsonencode()`. `{id}` is replaced with the resource ID (not in `create`).
